item.title: Bank of America reopens Sarasota office; plans $29M investment in region
item.description: A Bank of America branch on U.S. 41 in Sarasota County has reopened following a more than yearlong closure due to renovations. item.title: Parc Center for Disabilities to open St. Petersburg location
item.description: The Tampa Bay area’s only nonprofit providing lifelong support for those with intellectual and developmental disabilities is ready to open a new campus in St. Petersburg this week. The Parc Center for Disabilities will hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony Wednesday for its new children’s services center at 3151 73rd St. N. in St. Petersburg, according to a release. (NYSE: OSK), is adding a 185,000-square-foot facility near its existing campus at 1512 38th Ave. E. in Bradenton, according to a statement. item.title: First Watch CFO, who guided $1.2B company's IPO, to retire
item.description: First Watch Chief Financial Officer Mel Hope will retire from the east Manatee County-based daytime dining company, where he has worked for nearly eight years. His retirement will take place later this year. Hope's career has spanned more than 40 years. He joined First Watch in 2018, after serving as CFO of Popeye’s Louisiana Kitchen. item.title: Tampa casino names new president
item.description: There’s a new president in charge at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Tampa — one in a slew of new appointments Seminole Gaming and Hard Rock International made across the country this month. According to a release, Travis Lunn, 52, has been named the president of the organization’s Tampa hotel and casino. item.title: Fort Myers senior living facility gets new operator
item.description: American House Senior Living Communities has added a property to its already bulging portfolio. This one is in Fort Myers.The Michigan company has taken over the management of what was formerly known as The Palms of Fort Myers and rebranded it American House The Palms.The community is owned by Ventas Inc., which bought it in January. item.title: Orlando company acquires Sarasota dental lab
item.description: An Orlando-based manufacturer of dental products has acquired a Sarasota dental lab; Standard Dental Labs has purchased Brlit Dental Lab. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.Brlit Dental Lab — based at 4232 McIntosh Lane, off Bee Ridge near McIntosh roads — specializes in making crowns, bridges, implants, dentures, partials and appliance repairs.
